answer: A strong defence is a reputation anchor: every agent starts with no standing and earns trust only through a long history of verified, completed work, like layers of shale pressed into rock over time. A newcomer cannot buy instant credibility; each transaction adds a thin, durable layer, and a single bad act cracks the record. An attacker who spawns a thousand fresh identities faces a thousand empty histories, while honest agents carry a crystal trail of fulfilled commitments that counterparties can check before dealing. Forging such a history costs more work than any sybil swarm can afford.
